requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied tests and their assertions were enough to map each obligation. The `structural_hash` text is cited context, so I did not reassess it.

Obligations from `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, and the tests that cover them:

- **Path of segments, and the empty selector selects the root.**
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` parses `""` to an empty segment list.
  - It also parses a multi-segment path.
  - It rejects malformed selectors: `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]`, `fn[run]x`, and the empty segment in `a//b`.
  - `outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts that `resolve("")` returns 0, the root. It also checks that every produced selector resolves back to its own node.
- **Named segment is `kind[name]`.**
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` covers about twenty Rust kinds and nesting forms. Examples are `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.
  - Each selector is asserted both to be listed and to resolve to the node carrying that selector.
  - `profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent` checks that an unmapped node yields a "no outline node matches" error. It also checks that malformed escapes give an invalid-selector error.
- **Anonymous segment is `kind@hash`, with the first twelve hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts `use@` plus exactly 12 characters.
  - It shows that inserting siblings keeps the old selectors resolving, and that editing a node's own text invalidates only that node's selector.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` asserts that the selector equals `pair[items]/item@<first 12 of identity_hash>`. It also asserts that identity hash differs from structural hash. After a descendant edit the selector still resolves, and a child path beneath it resolves too.
  - The parse test checks hash normalisation and rejects a too-short hash (`use@123`).
- **`#N` disambiguation, one-based and in source order.**
  - `fn[repeated]#1` and `fn[repeated]#2` are produced and resolve.
  - Duplicate `use a::A;` nodes get `#1` and `#2`.
  - Unqualified `fn[repeated]` is rejected as ambiguous.
  - The parse test rejects `#0` and accepts `#2`.
- **`line` nodes are exempt from `#N`, and a line selector resolves when any line with that content exists.**
  - `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` shows two identical lines produce identical selectors.
  - That selector resolves, and the blank line is skipped.
  - Whitespace differences are ignored while joined words differ.
- **Percent-encoding of `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and whitespace as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are reversible.**
  - `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` asserts the exact encoded string. It covers every listed character, tab, a non-breaking space, an ideographic space, and the multibyte `é`.
  - It asserts that decoding restores the original name.
  - It asserts that unencoded `/` and space, and a bad `%zz` escape, are rejected.
  - The Rust test's `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` shows the encoding applied in real outline output.
  - `search.rs#fn[outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reinterpreting_resources]` checks that `mod[a%2Fb]` is accepted and that bad `%ZZ` and unterminated selectors are rejected.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** The insertion test in `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` shows selectors stay valid when lines shift. Selectors in every test are built only from kind, name, hash and ordinal.

I found no untested obligation and no marking gap. All the relevant tests carry a `{test}` reference to the requirement.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
